key_insight: In dilute polymer solutions, increasing polymer relaxation time shifts Lagrangian velocity attenuation from high to low frequencies and lengthens the Lagrangian integral timescale because polymers suppress vortical motion from small to large scales.
engineering_relevance: This helps predict and control turbulence transport and mixing in polymer processing, drag-reduction flows, and other viscoelastic fluid systems.
method: Direct numerical simulation of homogeneous isotropic turbulence with dilute polymer solutions
Varied Reynolds number, forcing method, and polymer relaxation time
Performed scale-decomposition of Lagrangian velocity to isolate contributions from vortices at different length scales
evidence_signal: The paper reports changes in the Lagrangian power spectral density and integral timescale across simulated conditions, linking these trends to scale-dependent vortex suppression.
watch_item: The conclusions come from DNS of homogeneous isotropic turbulence, so transfer to wall-bounded or strongly inhomogeneous industrial flows may require additional validation.
paper_title: Lagrangian velocity statistics of homogeneous isotropic turbulence in dilute polymer solutions
